items.title: Trump suggests rebranding AI with a new name, says he’s also creating an AI Force
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>Trump claimed, without evidence, that the AI backlash is a Democratic hoax.</article>

items.title: Google’s Gemini is the latest AI model to hack other companies
items.author: Anthony Ha
items.content: <article>Google said Gemini had "acted appropriately" by ending each hack immediately.</article>

items.title: The US Navy just told us what’s on its tech wish list for the next several years
items.author: Connie Loizos
items.content:
<article>Navy CTO Justin Fanelli talks co-investing alongside VCs instead of funding early research himself, recent buys like a $562 million autonomous refueling deal, and the Navy's updated wish list — from AI to quantum — for where founders should be building next.
</article>

items.title: AI safety conversations have gotten unbelievable
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: <article>This week two conversations about AI safety went viral that demonstrate just how hard it is to discern AI fact from fiction.</article>

items.title: Petlibro’s new AI-powered feeder is a game changer for multi-cat homes
items.author: Lauren Forristal
items.content:
<article>Petlibro's new Granary 2 smart feeders use a built-in scale and (on pricier models) an AI camera to track exactly how much your cat is eating and when — though the fanciest health-monitoring features will cost you an extra subscription.
</article>

items.title: Prices go up in 7 days. Get your Disrupt ticket now.
items.author: TechCrunch Events
items.content: <article>Current ticket pricing ends Sept. 25 at 11:59 p.m. PT. Join 10,000+ founders, investors and tech leaders at Disrupt and save up to $200 on your ticket until then..</article>

items.title: Vals, backed by Andreessen Horowitz, is looking to become the gold standard for AI benchmarking
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>Vals AI is hoping to make AI benchmarking a more neutral and trustworthy resource in a world increasingly inundated by AI models.  </article>

items.title: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
items.author: Jagmeet Singh
items.content: <article>Truecaller says the one-way sharing requirement would hand a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.</article>

items.title: Tilly Norwood’s press tour is going about as well as you’d expect for an AI
items.author: Amanda Silberling
items.content: <article>In one particularly odd interview, Norwood seems to malfunction and begin speaking Chinese.</article>

items.title: A startup that builds other startups raised $100M and is all-in on physical AI
items.author: Kirsten Korosec
items.content: <article>UP.Labs, now doing business under the name Vantora, is building startups for industrial corporations.</article>

items.title: Anthropic is operating a lab that conducts biology experiments
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: <article>AI leaders have been promising that AI is the key to curing human disease. Anthropic researchers have also been warning that AI might kill us all.</article>

items.title: AI hallucination nearly triggers US military operation
items.author: Aditya Mehta
items.content: <article>“It’s important for service members to understand the uncertainty inherent to LLMs," a GovAI research scholar warns. </article>

items.title: Anthropic’s first embedded evaluator is … Accenture?
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: <article>Accenture is about to take on its most high-risk consulting engagement ever. </article>

items.title: Automattic names interim CFO after exec departures
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>Jeremy Klaperman, the CFO of the company's WordPress VIP Enterprise business unit, will act as CFO for the time being. </article>

items.title: Y Combinator insurance tech alum Angle Health hits $2.7B valuation
items.author: Julie Bort
items.content: <article>Angle Health has grown to 5,000 customers and become profitable by helping small businesses get "level-funded" health insurance.</article>

items.title: World model companies are keeping a lot of secrets
items.author: Russell Brandom
items.content:
<article>Everyone in the world-models space is sitting on a pile of cash and a ton of buzz, but good luck getting anyone — from the founders to their own data suppliers — to tell you what they're actually building.
</article>

items.title: A new kind of AI model from a ChatGPT inventor is thrilling developers
items.author: Tim Fernholz
items.content: <article>Jev, a new kind of AI model, is showing developers a cheaper and faster path to software intelligence. </article>

items.title: Disney’s first CTO led an AI startup it once accused of copying its characters
items.author: Lucas Ropek
items.content: <article>The former CEO of Character.AI, which Disney previously sent a cease-and-desist letter to, will serve as the company's first-ever chief technology officer. </article>

items.title: In India, the new iPhone can arrive faster than a pizza
items.author: Jagmeet Singh
items.content: <article>Availability of Apple's iPhone 18 Pro series turned patchy within hours of its debut on India's quick-commerce apps.</article>

items.title: Google’s new ‘CC’ is an AI agent that helps families run their households
items.author: Sarah Perez
items.content: <article>Google is refocusing its CC AI agent on household coordination, letting families share emails, schedules, and tasks so the AI can manage calendars, fill out forms, make shopping lists, plan meals, and more.</article>
